title: warcraft-learner spec rulebook
description: AI-generated rulebook for a single WoW specialization. Extract all major offensive cooldowns, all personal defensive cooldowns, and the spec's checkable rotation/cooldown usage rules from the supplied guide content. Output ONLY the raw JSON object - no markdown fences, no preamble. The first character must be '{' and the last must be '}'.

spec.description: WCL spec name, e.g. SubtletyRogue. Must match the spec being analysed.

spec_icon.description: Required. The spec's zamimg icon file stem (no extension), e.g. 'ability_stealth'. Read it from the spec's guide page; it becomes the spec's dropdown art. Must be set on every rulebook.

major_cooldowns.description: REQUIRED and must be populated. All major cooldowns: abilities with a cooldown >= 30s that meaningfully affect damage output (or healing/tanking if applicable). Include on-use trinkets when the guide mentions specific timing for them. Every spec has at least one major cooldown, and most of the spec's analysis is driven from this list, so it must never be empty.

defensives.description: REQUIRED and must be populated. Every personal defensive cooldown with a cooldown >= 15s: immunities, absorb shields, significant damage reductions (>= 20%), and meaningful self-heals. Do NOT include passive talents or stance toggles.

rules.description: The spec's rotation and cooldown rules, each one something the app can check against a player's own log: which abilities go together, which buffs and dots stay up, which resource level to spend at, how many enemies change the priority, and what the opener is. Every rule needs a condition, so leave out advice that cannot be expressed as one of the condition kinds - a spec whose sources are mostly prose yields few rules, which is correct. Quality over count: two real rules beat eight, and an empty list is valid. Never write a 'keep X on cooldown' rule; the app already checks that for every major cooldown.

source_summary.description: 2-3 sentences summarising the cooldown strategy these guides recommend.

guide_count.description: Written by the pipeline after the rulebook is saved. Never populate it.

saved_at.description: Written by the pipeline after the rulebook is saved. Never populate it.

name.description: Exact ability name as it appears in-game.

spell_id.description: WoW spell ID - REQUIRED. Prioritize the Active Ability Cast ID rather than a passive Aura, Classic WoW ID, or Talent Node ID. Verify at wowhead.com/spell=<id>. If genuinely unsure, supply your best guess and record the uncertainty in id_note - NEVER in usage_rule, which is shown to users as coaching copy.

duration.description: Optional. Active buff/window duration in seconds.

align_with_bloodlust.description: true if the guide explicitly says to sync this with Bloodlust / Heroism / Time Warp. Default false if the guide does not mention it.

opener_priority.description: Optional. Cast order in the opener (1 = first). Only set if the guide specifies a sequence.

usage_rule.description: One sentence: when and how to use this cooldown.

id_note.description: Optional. Internal maintainer note for any spell-ID uncertainty (e.g. 'best guess for the Midnight X cast, verify on Wowhead'). NEVER shown to users and not read by any analysis - put verification/best-guess notes here instead of in usage_rule.

talent_gated.description: Optional. Set to true when this ability requires a specific talent that not all builds take. When true, having zero casts is treated as normal rather than a 'never used' error.

spell_id.description: WoW spell ID - REQUIRED, same rule as major_cooldowns.

usage_rule.description: One sentence: when/why to press this button.

id_note.description: Optional. Internal maintainer note for any spell-ID uncertainty (e.g. 'best guess for the Midnight X cast, verify on Wowhead'). NEVER shown to users and not read by any analysis - put verification/best-guess notes here instead of in usage_rule.

talent_gated.description: Optional. Set to true when this ability requires a specific talent that not all builds take.

type.description: Rule category. cooldown_pairing: two abilities must be cast together or in sequence. cd_hold: an ability should be delayed until an anchor cooldown is available. opener: specific sequence or timing required at pull. rotation: ongoing priority or combo maintained throughout the fight. aoe_switch: behavior changes when multiple targets are present.

severity.description: How hard the app presses the player when they break this rule. critical: ignoring it fundamentally breaks the spec. warning: a real DPS loss worth fixing. info: an optimization worth knowing about. These are the exact three tiers the findings table renders, so write the one the coaching deserves.

description.description: Short rule title the player sees, naming the abilities rather than the check, e.g. 'Secret Technique always inside Shadow Dance'. Shown both when the rule is broken and when it is followed, so write the rule itself, not a complaint. 60 characters is what the findings table renders untruncated.

condition.description: REQUIRED. How the app checks this rule against the player's log. Pick the kind that matches what the rule actually says rather than forcing it into a nearby one: a rule about a buff being up wants castOutsideBuff or auraUptimeBelow, a resource level wants resourceAtCast, a target count wants castAtTargetCount, an opener wants openingSequence, which of two fillers to press in a given state wants fillerInBuff, a stacking buff spent like a resource wants spendAtStacks, a damage-over-time effect refreshed too early wants auraClipped, and the ability that takes over in execute range wants fillerBelowHealth. A rule that fits none of them does not belong in the rulebook. Each kind takes ability identities and a direction only - never a number: the app measures every threshold a rule is judged against from the encounter's best logs, so a rule that carries no numbers adapts to a fight the field plays differently instead of failing the player against a guess. The source's concrete numbers belong in the rule's action text.

action.description: Second-person instruction telling the player what to DO, not describing what the check found. This is where the sources' concrete numbers belong - thresholds, target counts, hold windows - since the condition itself carries none. Good: 'Always cast Secret Technique inside Shadow Dance, at 5+ combo points.' Bad: 'Shadow Dance was cast without Secret Technique beforehand.'

castWithoutPrior.description: Use when the sources say two abilities go together: 'always X inside Y', 'send Y then X'. Do not write a pairing window.

spell_id.description: The ability being coached. Every cast of it is either a pass or a violation.

spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

required_spell_id.description: The companion ability that must accompany it. Under the default position 'before' the companion is the one cast FIRST, so for 'Secret Technique always inside Shadow Dance' the companion is Shadow Dance.

required_spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

position.description: Which side the companion sits on. 'before' (the default) is what most rules mean. 'after' when the sources say the companion follows. 'either' only when they say pair or sync without naming an order. Read the rule's own action text back against this before writing it.

holdCooldownForAnchor.description: Use when the sources say to save one ability for a bigger one: 'hold X for Y', 'do not spend X before Y'. Do not write a hold time.

spell_ids.description: The abilities that should be saved. List every one the sources name for this anchor.

spell_names.description: Exact in-game names, one per entry of spell_ids and in the same order.

anchor_spell_id.description: The bigger cooldown they are being saved for.

anchor_spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

castOutsideBuff.description: Use when the sources tie an ability to a buff being active rather than to another cast: 'only during Metamorphosis', 'never while Darkest Night is up'. Prefer this over castWithoutPrior whenever the rule names a buff, since a buff can outlast or precede the cast that granted it. Needs no numbers at all.

spell_id.description: The ability being coached. Every cast of it is either a pass or a violation.

spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

buff_spell_id.description: The buff or form whose presence decides each cast. Use the aura's own id, which is often not the id of the ability that applies it.

buff_spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

require.description: 'inside' for 'only cast it while the buff is up', which flags casts made while it is down. 'outside' for 'never cast it while the buff is up'.

auraUptimeBelow.description: Use for the 'keep X up' family: a buff or a damage-over-time effect the sources say should never fall off. Do not write a target percentage.

aura_spell_id.description: The buff or damage-over-time effect that must stay up. Use the aura's own id, not the id of a different ability that refreshes it.

aura_spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

on.description: 'self' for a buff on the player. 'target' for anything the player keeps on enemies, which covers almost every damage-over-time rule.

openingSequence.description: Use when the sources give a specific opening order: 'open with X, then Y, then Z'. Extra casts between the listed steps are allowed, so list only the abilities whose order actually matters. Do not write a time limit.

spell_ids.description: The opener abilities, in the order the sources say to cast them.

spell_names.description: Exact in-game names, one per entry of spell_ids and in the same order.

castAtTargetCount.description: Use for the AoE switch: an ability the sources say to start using on several targets, or to stop using once several are up. Do not write a target count, even when the guide names one - put that number in the rule's action text instead.

spell_id.description: The ability whose use depends on how many enemies are up.

spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

bound.description: 'min' for an ability only worth pressing on several targets, which flags using it on too few. 'max' for a single-target ability that should give way to a cleave, which flags using it on too many.

resourceAtCast.description: Use when the sources gate an ability on a resource level: 'spend at 5 combo points', 'never overcap Soul Shards'. Do not write an amount, even when the guide names one - put that number in the rule's action text instead.

spell_id.description: The ability whose use depends on the resource level.

spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

resource_type.description: The resource's numeric power type: 0 mana, 1 rage, 2 focus, 3 energy, 4 combo points, 6 runic power, 7 soul shards, 8 astral power, 9 holy power, 11 maelstrom, 12 chi, 13 insanity, 17 fury, 18 pain, 19 essence.

resource_name.description: The resource's name in lower case, used in the coaching copy the player reads, e.g. 'combo points'.

bound.description: 'min' for a spender that should only go off at a high resource level, which flags spending too low. 'max' for a generator that should not be pressed near the cap, which is how an overcap rule is written.

procWasted.description: Use for a proc the sources say to consume on sight: 'spend Hot Streak immediately', 'react to Nightfall'. Flags every time the proc expired with none of the spend abilities cast. Needs no numbers at all.

buff_spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

spend_spell_ids.description: The abilities that consume the proc. Casting any one of them while it is up counts as spending it, so list every option the sources name.

spend_spell_names.description: Exact in-game names, one per entry of spend_spell_ids and in the same order.

fillerInBuff.description: Use for the filler choice: a spec that builds with one spell while a state is up and a different one otherwise, 'Wrath in Solar Eclipse', 'Demonbolt on Demonic Core'. Judged as a share of the fillers cast inside the state, so prefer it over castOutsideBuff whenever the judged spell is a filler. Do not write a share. Exclusions are required here, not optional: an omitted list cannot be told apart from a deliberate empty one, and a missed suspending state accuses correct play.

spell_id.description: The filler that should dominate while the buff is up.

spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

alternative_spell_ids.description: The competing filler(s) it should displace in this state. List every filler the spec would otherwise press, since the check reads the share of this pool rather than a raw count.

alternative_spell_names.description: Exact in-game names, one per entry of alternative_spell_ids and in the same order.

buff_spell_id.description: The buff or state that decides the choice. Use the aura's own id, which is often not the id of the ability that grants it.

buff_spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

except_buff_spell_ids.description: REQUIRED; [] is a valid answer. Aura ids for the states that suspend the choice, whose casts drop out of the share entirely. Name every burst window granting both states at once and every proc the sources say to press the other filler under. Write [] only after replaying the rule against the sampled parses and finding none.

except_buff_spell_names.description: Exact in-game names, one per entry of except_buff_spell_ids and in the same order.

spendAtStacks.description: Use when the sources gate an ability on a stacking buff rather than on a class resource: 'spend at 5 Maelstrom Weapon', 'never cap Arcane Charges'. Do not write a stack count, even when the guide names one - put that number in the rule's action text instead.

spell_id.description: The spender for bound min, or the generator for bound max.

spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

buff_spell_id.description: The stacking buff that acts as the resource. Use the aura's own id, which is often not the id of the ability that grants it.

buff_spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

bound.description: min flags spending below the count the field waits for; max flags generating while the buff is already near its cap.

except_buff_spell_ids.description: Optional. Aura ids for the states that suspend the rule, whose casts are excluded entirely. Name the procs the sources say license a cheap cast, or the rule reads correct play as a violation.

except_buff_spell_names.description: Exact in-game names, one per entry of except_buff_spell_ids and in the same order.

auraClipped.description: Use for the 'do not clip X' family: a damage-over-time effect the sources say to refresh late rather than early. Only refreshes the player cast are judged, since most refreshes in a log are procs. Do not write a pandemic window.

aura_spell_id.description: The aura as the log records it, which is regularly a different id from the cast that applies it.

aura_spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

cast_spell_id.description: The cast that applies the aura. Usually shares its name with the aura and differs in id, so take both from the table rather than reusing one.

cast_spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

on.description: target reads the enemy debuff stream, which is where damage-over-time rules live; self reads the player's own buffs.

except_buff_spell_ids.description: Optional. Aura ids for the states that suspend the rule, whose refreshes are excluded entirely. Name the cooldowns the sources say to re-snapshot the effect under, or the rule reads correct play as a violation.

except_buff_spell_names.description: Exact in-game names, one per entry of except_buff_spell_ids and in the same order.

fillerBelowHealth.description: Use for the execute switch: an ability the sources say replaces your filler below a health threshold, 'Execute under 20%', 'Kill Shot in execute range'. Write health_pct, which is the ability's own game constant rather than a field behaviour, and no other number.

spell_id.description: The execute ability that should take over below the threshold.

spell_name.description: The exact in-game ability name for the id above. Both come from the prepared ability table.

alternative_spell_ids.description: The filler(s) it should displace down there. List every filler the spec would otherwise press, since the check reads the share of this pool rather than a raw count.

alternative_spell_names.description: Exact in-game names, one per entry of alternative_spell_ids and in the same order.

health_pct.description: The ability's own execute threshold as a percentage, e.g. 20 or 35 with Massacre. Read it from the tooltip for the build the field plays; it is a game constant like a cooldown, not something to estimate from parses.

except_buff_spell_ids.description: Optional. Aura ids for the states that suspend the choice, whose casts are excluded entirely. Name the burst windows that override the execute priority, or the rule reads correct play as a violation.

except_buff_spell_names.description: Exact in-game names, one per entry of except_buff_spell_ids and in the same order.
